content.text: : herpes labialis (cold sores) · gingivostomatitis · pharyngotonsillitis · herpetic whitlow · herpetic gladiatorum · keratitis · conjunctivitis · blepharitis · aseptic meningitis · encephalitis
(vulva, vagina, cervix, glans, prepuce, penile shaft) - “below the waist”
Both HSV-1 & -2 can affect oral or genital regions - genital herpes MC ← HSV-2 but HSV-1 ↑freq
Transmission: direct contact w skin · sores · body fluids - oral sex = common (oral ↔ genital)
Genital infect: primary (⍉HSV Ab → infected w HSV-1 or -2) · nonprimary (HSV-1 Ab → infected w HSV-2 or vice versa) · recurr (lesion HSV type = same as serum Ab)
Recurr much more likely w HSV-2 than HSV-1
Latency: in sensory nerve ganglia (trigeminal → face/oral · sacral root → genital) - reactivation ← ↑fever · trauma · physical/emotional stress · sunlight · menstruation

Shedding w active infect (± lesions) - transmission: close personal contact - HSV-1 USU acquired in childhood (oral secretions) - HSV-2: sexual activity (poss sexual abuse in young children) · vaginal delivery w active maternal infect
Most aSx - IS: more severe dz · comp · reactivation → dissemination (esp impaired T-cell immunity)
Latency sites: HSV = neurons · EBV (gammaherpesvirus) = B cells · CMV = myeloid progenitor cells · HIV (retrovirus) = T cells
systemic sxs · longer · greater risk of comp
grouped vesicles on an erythematous base
•gingivostomatitis: MC HSV infect in children & MC primary HSV manifestation - 6mo–5y - HSV-1 (many spreaders aSx)
•prodrome: abrupt ↑fever · anorexia · malaise · irritability · restlessness · sleeplessness · HA

•gingivitis (swollen erythematous gums that bleed easily) · vesicles on gingiva · labial & buccal mucosa · tongue · hard palate · pharynx · perioral → ulcerate & coalesce - ruptured vesicles yellow w red halos · tender regional LAD
•lasts up to 2wks → latent in trigeminal ganglion → recurr stomatitis or herpes labialis
•comp: dehydration (MC - ↓PO intake) · herpetic whitlow · herpetic keratitis
Recurr: localized burning/paresthesias may precede w.o constitutional sxs - some pts ⍉lesions
Eczema herpeticum: also an HSV site infect
•conjunctival injection · dendritic lesions on fluorescein stain
: vesicles on lid margin · chemosis · eyelid edema · tearing

Genital: primary more severe than nonprimary/recurr - painful or pruritic lesions · tender inguinal LAD · may be aSx - prodrome: fever · HA · myalgias · mild tingling where lesions appear - clustered vesicles on erythematous base rupture → ulcers w scalloped borders → crust over
: viral cx · PCR · direct fluorescence Ab · type-specific serology · Tzank (multinucleated giant cells)
•genital lesions/vesicles present: PCR preferred (more sensitive than viral cx · distinguishes HSV-1 vs -2) - viral cx ↓sensitivity - esp crusted/healing lesions
•crusted lesions or ⍉vesicular fluid: swab for PCR still preferred - serology for HSV Ab if ⍉lesions

•serology: recurr/atypical lesions w ⊖PCR/cx or clin dx w.o lab confirmation - ⍉proves current lesions = HSV (Ab may reflect prev infect) · HSV-1 Ab ⍉distinguish oral vs genital · may be undetectable early
•Tzanck: rapid · inexpensive - ↓sensitivity · ⍉distinguish HSV-1 vs HSV-2 vs VZV
•gingivostomatitis/labialis: dx clin - confirm w PCR or cx · immunofluorescence · Tzanck
•PCR more sensitive than cx - preferred for CNS (HSV encephalitis) or eye infect
•direct fluorescent Ag: ulcer bases or cx cells - Ab testing → seroconversion
•topical analgesics: severely painful lesions · sitz baths: women w severe dysuria
•chronic suppressive tx: very freq/severe recurr or to ↓transmission to partner
•⍉sexual activity w prodrome or active lesions - even w barrier contraception
•preg: acyclovir or valacyclovir x7-10d after primary infect & from 36wks → delivery - C-section if active genital lesions @ delivery
Gingivostomatitis: supportive (hydration · pain control) - PO acyclovir if immunocompetent & w.in 96h + unable to drink or severe pain - all IS children → acyclovir
Labialis: ⍉tx or episodic or chronic suppression w PO antiviral (acyclovir) - topical better suited for labialis
•antivirals = mainstay - topical · PO · IV by severity & site
•long-term suppressive PO acyclovir/valacyclovir: freq recurr · IS pts
•severe infect · IS · HSV encephalitis: empiric ↑dose IV acyclovir
